problem: VLMs perform well on passive offline image/video understanding but fail in closed-loop embodied settings (short-sighted exploration, spatial-semantic drift as the viewpoint changes, forgetting targets that leave the field of view). Existing embodied datasets lack step-wise reasoning annotations, online closed-loop interaction, or photorealism.
motivation: Embodied agents must act from egocentric views where each action changes the next observation, which passive video pretraining never teaches. A pilot study with GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-VL found consistent failure patterns, motivating a dataset with step-level reasoning traces aligned to perception and action.
key_idea: Build EmbRACE-3K, a dataset of about 3k language-guided Unreal Engine tasks with human demonstrations and step-wise Gemini-generated reasoning, and use it to benchmark VLMs and to train Qwen2.5-VL-7B with SFT followed by GRPO.
insight: Step-wise reasoning supervision helps: the SFT variant with think traces beats the no-thinking variant on out-of-domain Dynamic Spatial-Semantic (SR 35.6 vs 27.1) and Multi-stage (18.9 vs 10.8). SFT alone overfits in-domain (Exploration SR 71.4 in-domain vs 22.8 out-of-domain), and adding GRPO improves out-of-domain SR (Exploration 30.9, Multi-stage 27.0). The no-thinking variant is far more efficient (fewer steps and timeouts) but generalizes worse.
method: Simulation platform: UnrealCV-Zoo on Unreal Engine; 24 of 100 photorealistic indoor and outdoor maps selected for diversity.
Stage 1 pose sampling: automated sampling with the Navigation Movement API plus manual filtering of trivial or unreachable spots; records 6-DoF pose and egocentric RGB.

Stage 2 instruction generation: Gemini 2.5 Pro receives the RGB view plus nearby object metadata and a target task type (Basic, Exploration, Dynamic Spatial-Semantic, Multi-stage, Interaction), followed by manual verification and human-authored additions.
Stage 3 human demonstration: a human player executes each instruction in real time; egocentric frames, actions and poses are recorded; trajectories longer than 32 steps are filtered out.
Stage 4 reasoning annotation: Gemini sees the instruction, all frames and the full action trajectory and writes a natural-language rationale for each step; the result is about 3k tasks and 26k steps.
SFT: Qwen2.5-VL-7B fine-tuned in LLaMA-Factory on 2,344 trajectories (about 10k actions) as multi-turn dialogue, outputting <think>...</think><action>...</action>.
RL: GRPO in the R1V framework with G=6, rule-based format and action-accuracy rewards, applied after SFT.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B (SFT then GRPO fine-tuned); baselines GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Pro (frozen)
setting.training_data: EmbRACE-3K: 2,344 reasoning trajectories (~10k actions) for SFT, then GRPO on the same dataset; Gemini-generated instructions and rationales with human demonstrations
setting.observation: egocentric RGB: current frame, five most recent frames and initial frame, plus task instruction, brief scene description and action history
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (MoveForward, TurnLeft, etc., plus look, interact, Finish), max 32 steps

numbers.extra: SFT + GRPO on EmbRACE-3K; in-domain scenes

numbers_note: Only the sft-rl (main) rows are given for all six task types (Interaction Open Door and Pick&Drop omitted above). The text lists no separate benchmark name; 'other:EmbRACE-3K' with in-domain/out-of-domain test tasks is used, and the split label 'test' is an assumption. Interaction results are in Table 2 (Open Door in-domain SR 73.6, out-of-domain 45.5; Pick&Drop in-domain SR 50.0, out-of-domain 37.5). The text discussion contains internal inconsistencies with the tables (e.g. some 'in-domain' numbers cited are out-of-domain).
results: Zero-shot GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-7B are weak on Exploration, Spatial-Semantic and Multi-stage tasks, especially out-of-domain (GPT-4o SR 3.6, 10.2 and 2.7 respectively). The SFT+RL Qwen2.5-VL-7B reaches out-of-domain SR 30.9 (Exploration), 42.4 (Dynamic Spatial-Semantic) and 27.0 (Multi-stage), above Gemini 2.5 Pro (9.1, 20.3, 16.2) and GPT-4o. SFT-only overfits in-domain, and RL narrows the generalization gap.
limitations: Small, specific evaluation set (in-domain splits appear to be a few dozen episodes per type) and only Unreal Engine simulation, with no real-robot tests; the text also has inconsistencies between the discussed and tabulated numbers
Out-of-domain generalization is still limited (SR 27-53%), and the paper only provides basic supervised and GRPO baselines with rule-based rewards
Rationales are generated by Gemini after seeing the whole trajectory, which may introduce hindsight bias; the input uses a limited frame window (current, last five, first)
